name: DefineHumanPlayerGeneral

retail.prototype_evidence: Binary Ninja reports an x87-confused prototype; the observed stack use is a first argument that receives a six-dword result block (rep movsd, ecx=6, at 0x004101AD) and a frame argument read as [esp+0x34] at 0x00410075. The script VM's native-call site 0x004BD8F3-0x004BD8FE pushes exactly three dwords (the VM value-block slot, the symbol record's +0x18 dword, the argument frame) and copies six dwords from the returned EAX, which fixes the layout as (void* context, int32_t unused, void* frame) returning context.
retail.registrar: Registered at 0x0041001B through 0x004B8890 as DefineHumanPlayerGeneral with argc bounds (0, -1); it has no static callers and is invoked from the script VM.

return_block.copy: rep movsd x6 to the first argument

retail.behavior: Nine script arguments are read through 0x004B8A50 and stored with the retail scaling at 0x0056E1E8..0x0056E208; the next 34 arguments fill the first dword of two 17-entry 0x10-stride tables; the 0x18-byte value block is copied to the caller's context, which is returned.

previous_audit_errors: The earlier audit said index 0 is also stored at 0x0056E208. The store at 0x00410137 is index 8 (push 8 at 0x0041012F); 0x0056E204 is index 7 and 0x0056E208 is index 8, so the block holds nine distinct values and there is no second copy of index 0.
The earlier audit described the old candidate, which took a float array and a count and never called 0x004B8A50.

findings: The corrected candidate reads the same 43 argument indices in the same order through Qvm_GetFloatArg.
It applies the same four constants in the same x87 precision and the same store order, and writes the same nine dwords and two tables.
It builds the same 24-byte return block and returns the context argument.
The second stack argument is unused in retail and in the candidate.
documented_differences: +0x04 of the returned block is zero in the candidate and stack residue in retail.
std::rintl supplies fistp's rounding under the current control word, which makes the compiler add a control-word save, frndint and a restore around the conversion.
Retail's table-B base set-up block is folded into the candidate's table-B loop.

limitations: No paired retail/candidate runtime capture exists for this address.
